statement_spans.source_role: Complete original Exercise6.88, the single counted target: for a binary tree G and a subdivision law nu whose tail decays slower than exponentially, Phi*_E(G) > 0 yet Phi*_E(G_nu) = 0 a.s., with G_nu the Section 6.9 random subdivision.

proof_spans.source_role: Original Exercise 6.88 with its complete printed author Comment on physical p. 638: the failure of an exponential tail gives P[sum_{i<=n} L_i >= cn] >= P[L_1 >= cn] >= e^{-eps n} for infinitely many n; the 2^n pairwise disjoint level-n-to-level-2n paths of the binary tree give, by union bound, 1 - (1-e^{-eps n})^{2^n} >= 1 - exp(-e^{-eps n} 2^n) -> 1; a good path extended to the root gives |d_E S| / sum_{e in E(S)} L_e <= (2n+1)/(cn) ~ 2/c; and since c is arbitrary the closing display asserts the vanishing of the anchored constant a.s. The uncounted context reprints the anchored constants of physical p. 234, the edge-set notation (6.33) of physical p. 217, the random-subdivision and exponential-tail definitions with Phi**_E and Theorem 6.50 on physical p. 238, and the necessity remark that cites the exercise on physical p. 240. No author step is expanded or repaired, no constant is synchronised and no hypothesis is altered.

scope_conventions: The single a.s. conclusion of Exercise 6.88 for a binary tree with the root o as basepoint and a subdivision law on the positive integers with no exponential tail: the anchored edge-expansion constant of the random subdivision is 0 a.s. The companion clause Phi*_E(G) > 0 is the standing positive-expansion property of the base tree and is not a second target; the necessity remark on physical p. 240 and Theorem 6.50 on physical p. 238 are the body statements the exercise is attached to and are not counted again. No general tree, no other subdivision law and no other exercise.
literal_source_feature: Measured, not inherited: the constant printed on physical p. 252 in the question and in the closing display of the Comment on physical p. 638 carries exactly one raised script-size asterisk at 6.30 pt per occurrence (p. 252: three occurrences, none with two; p. 638: one occurrence, none with two), while the double-star symbol occurs only on physical pp. 238 and 240, set as two raised asterisks at 7.35 pt, and the unanchored constant of Exercise 6.23 on physical p. 238 has no asterisk at all. The owner material review, the independent material review and the owner adjudication all describe the printed link between this exercise and the body as the inequality Phi**_E <= Phi*_E, which is a misreading of the double-star symbol; those three reports are left unedited and the measured reading is recorded here. The printed link that does close the Comment's last step is the tree equality Phi**_E(G) = Phi*_E(G) printed on physical p. 238, which the adjudication itself states. The Comment's denominators are kept as printed: L_e and sum_{e in E(S)} L_e over the edge set E(S), and partial_E S over the vertex set S.
